chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Lays al-Muradi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man travels during the month of Ramadan, he should break his fast; and if he were to fast it out of ignorance, he would not make it up.

key_terms.قَضَى: To make up (a missed obligatory act)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler fasts during Ramadan out of ignorance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a traveler’s voluntary fasting during Ramadan, when done out of ignorance of the exemption, is valid and does not require make-up (qada), reflecting the principle that ignorance excuses the obligation rather than invalidating the act. It highlights the juristic distinction between the validity of the act (sahih) and the obligation to perform it (wujub), a key nuance in Shia fiqh. The ruling underscores the mercy in Islamic law by not penalizing those who act in good faith but lack specific legal knowledge.

en.hubeali:
Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Lays Al Murady, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man travels during a Month of Ramazan, he should break (not Fast); and if he were to Fast it out of ignorance, he would not make up for it’.
en.sarwar: 3. From Safwan ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Layth al-Muradiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one travels in the month of Ramadan he must stop fasting; but if he fasts because of ignorance, he is not required to complete its Qada’ (compensatory fast).”
